literal: Having studied, and having understood, and having taught to others, oneself not self-controlled, than [that] fool, fools do not exist.
translation: There are no fools greater than those who, despite having studied, understood, and taught others, fail to practice self-control themselves.
modern: நூல்களைப் படித்து, அவற்றின் பொருளை உணர்ந்து, பிறருக்கும் எடுத்துச் சொல்லியும், தான் மட்டும் அதன்படி அடங்கி நடக்காத பேதையை விடப் பெரிய பேதையர் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate form of foolishness. A person might acquire vast book knowledge, comprehend its deeper meaning, and even eloquently preach it to others. However, if they fail to govern their own conduct according to that knowledge, their learning is useless. The poet emphasizes that there is no greater fool than someone who knows the right path but refuses to walk it.
